questions.q: In a contest held all over the country, 185 contestants won prizes after participating in the final round. 60% of the contestants could not make it to the final round. If 63% of the people participating in the final round did not win any prizes, then how many people participated in the contest?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, final round mein prize nahi jeetne wale $63\%$ hain, matlab jeetne wale bache $37\%$. Unki value $185$ (exact $5 \times 37$) di hai. Mentally reverse chal.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Reverse chain method laga bina kisi variable (x) ke. Mathematically :-

$\text{Final Winners } \% = 100 - 63 = 37\%$

$37\% = 185 \Rightarrow 100\% (\text{Finalists}) = 500$

$\text{Made to Final } \% = 100 - 60 = 40\%$

$40\% \text{ of Total} = 500$

$\text{Total} = \frac{500 \times 100}{40} = 1250$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable tree lagakar single equation solve kar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Total} = x$

$\text{Finalists} = 0.40x$

$\text{Winners} = 0.37 \times (0.40x) = 185$

$0.148x = 185$

$x = \frac{185}{0.148} = 1250$

Exam Takeaway: Jaha value chain ke end mein di ho waha backwards jana aur seedhi values banana best hota hai.

questions.q: In a corporate restructuring, the total number of employees in Division A and Division B remains strictly constant. Initially, Division A has '$x$' more employees than Division B, and it is given that Division A has exactly $13x$ employees. After a transfer drive, Division B becomes the majority with '$5x$' more employees than Division A. Meanwhile, the average revenue generated per employee in Division B increased from ₹7,12,400 to ₹8,54,880. What is the exact percentage change in the total revenue generated by Division B?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM (Constant Sum Shifting) + Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yeh hai TCS ka asli jaal! Total Revenue = (No. of Employees) $\times$ (Revenue per Employee). Yahan multiply ho raha hai, toh end mein Successive (Theory 2) lagega. Lekin Division B ke employees ka increase directly nahi diya, usko unhone Theory 1 ($A+B=K$) mein chhupa diya hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dono ka percentage shift nikal aur formula me daal de! Employee shift JSM se find kar, baki direct observation.

Mathematically :-
$$ A - B = x \\implies B = 13x - x = 12x \\\\ Gap = x - (-5x) = 6x \\\\ \\Delta Emp = \\frac{6x}{2} = 3x \\\\ \\% \\Delta Emp = \\frac{3x}{12x} = 25\\% \\\\ \\% \\Delta Rev/Emp = \\frac{854880 - 712400}{712400} = 20\\% \\\\ Net = 25 + 20 + \\frac{25 \\times 20}{100} = 50\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute revenue variables generate kar initial stage aur final stage me aur shift detect kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ Rev_1 = 12x \\times 712400 \\\\ Rev_2 = 15x \\times 854880 \\\\ \\frac{Rev_2}{Rev_1} = \\frac{15}{12} \\times \\frac{854880}{712400} = 1.25 \\times 1.2 = 1.5 \\\\ \\Delta = 50\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi do concepts mix hon, unko isolation mein solve kar. Total number ya exact variables ($x$) nikalne ki koshish mat kar, hamesha base fractional values aur percentages pe khel.

questions.q:
A massive commercial cargo ship has a strictly fixed maximum payload capacity dedicated entirely to carrying only two types of containers: Type-A (Chemicals) and Type-B (Textiles). The total payload weight of a container type is determined by multiplying the "Weight per container" by the "Number of containers". Initially, the total payload weight of Type-A was exactly 33.33% of the total payload weight of Type-B.

Due to new safety regulations, the weight of "each" Type-A container is increased by 15%, while the company strictly keeps the number of Type-A containers unchanged. To keep the ship's total payload weight exactly at its fixed maximum capacity, by what percentage must the overall payload weight of Type-B containers be reduced?
questions.s: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Layer 1: Constant Base Expansion: Weight/Box $\times$ No. of Boxes = Total Weight ($A \times B = K$). Layer 2: JSM / The Zero-Sum Game: Total Weight A + Total Weight B = Fixed Ship Capacity ($A + B = K$). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai, dimaag ko bilkul shant rakh. SSC wale language badal ke darayenge, par core engine wahi hai. Type-A containers $33.33\%$ hain Type-B ke. Yani Ratio $1:3$ hai. Type-A ke har ek dabbe ka wazan $15\%$ badha aur dabbon ki sankhya same rahi (Layer 1). Iska seedha sa matlab hai ki Type-A ka Total Wazan exact $15\%$ se badh gaya! Ab total jahaz ka wazan fix rakhna hai, toh Type-A ne jitna wazan badhaya, Type-B ko exactly utna hi wazan kam karna padega (Layer 2). 10 second ka game hai! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Ratio Balancer): Ratio of Total Weights $\rightarrow$ Type-A : Type-B = $1 : 3$. Type-A ka naya gain = $1$ unit ka $15\%$ = $+0.15$ units. Kyuki Jahaz ka total wazan (Capacity) fix hai, jo wazan Type-A ne gain kiya, wo Type-B ko lose karna padega. Type-B ka reduction = $-0.15$ units. Percentage Reduction in Type-B = $\frac{\text{Actual Reduction}}{\text{Type-B Base}} \times 100$ $\Rightarrow \frac{0.15}{3} \times 100 =$ $5\%$. Option 2 is strictly correct. Method 2 (Concept Builder - Assumption Method): Let Total Weight of Type-B = $300$ tons. Since Type-A is $33.33\%$ (or $1/3$) of B, Type-A = $100$ tons. Total Ship Capacity = $100 + 300 = 400$ tons. Type-A ka wazan $15\%$ badh gaya $\Rightarrow$ Naya Type-A = $115$ tons. Ship capacity $400$ fix rakhni hai, toh Naya Type-B = $400 - 115 = 285$ tons. Type-B mein kitni girawat aayi? $300 \rightarrow 285$, yani $15$ tons ki girawat aayi $300$ par. Percentage = $\frac{15}{300} \times 100 =$ $5\%$. Future Exam Takeaway: Language chahe "Cargo Capacity" ki ho ya "Server/Data Bandwidth" ki, agar ek component $A \times B$ se bana hai aur unka overall sum fixed hai, toh direct base ratio likho aur shift ko transfer kar do. Ye Double-Engine hacks hi top rankers ka secret weapon hain!

questions.q: The present population of a village is 45,840. If the number of males increases by $25\%$ and that of females increases by $15\%$, then the population will become 55,284. What is the difference between the initial number of males and females in the village?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, isme Mixture Alligation ya phir Base Shifting lagate hain. Maan le pura gaon hi $15\%$ se badh gaya hota. Total kitna badhta? Jo extra badha hai woh sirf Males ke bache hue $10\%$ ka kamaal hai.

Method 1 (Base Shifting Concept):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Actual Increase} = 55284 - 45840 = 9444 \\ \text{Base } 15\% \text{ Increase} = 45840 \times 15\% = 6876 \\ \text{Extra Increase} = 9444 - 6876 = 2568 \\ 10\% \text{ of } M = 2568 \implies M = 25680 \\ F = 45840 - 25680 = 20160 \\ M - F = 25680 - 20160 = 5520 $$

Exam Takeaway: Base Shifting wali trick CDS aur CGL dono ke time consuming mixture problems ko crush karti hai.

questions.q: Sushil's monthly salary is 20% of Pankaj's annual salary. Yash's monthly salary is 3/4th of Sushil's monthly salary. If the monthly salary of Pankaj is Rs 15000, what is the annual salary of Yash?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Equating units to real values)

Pen-Free Observation: Pankaj ki monthly 15k hai, toh chain reaction me Yash ki annual kafi badi aayegi. Pura khela sirf clear base-shifting ka hai. Question ke keywords 'Monthly' aur 'Annual' ko dhyan se dekhna hai aur single line me execution karna hai. Maximum bacche ratio me Pankaj ki annual value ko uski monthly se equate karke Concept Leakage kar dete hain!

Method 1 (The Chain Reaction - Exam Approach):
Aise simple chain problems me ratio banake time waste mat kar. Jab clear percentage aur fraction diye hon, toh peeche se single line execution kar:
  • Pankaj (Monthly) = 15,000
  • Pankaj (Annual) = 15,000 $\times$ 12 = 1,80,000
  • Sushil (Monthly) = 20% of Pankaj (Annual) = $\frac{1}{5} \times 1,80,000 = 36,000$
  • Yash (Monthly) = $\frac{3}{4}$ of Sushil (Monthly) = $\frac{3}{4} \times 36,000 = 27,000$
  • Yash (Annual) = 27,000 $\times$ 12 = 3,24,000


Method 2 (Ratio Scaling Correction):
Agar tu ratio banata hai $S : P(\text{Annual}) : Y = 4 : 20 : 3$, toh yaad rakh 20 units Pankaj ki Annual salary hai, monthly nahi.
Pankaj (Annual) = 15,000 $\times$ 12 = 1,80,000.
So, 20 units = 1,80,000 $\implies$ 1 unit = 9,000.
Yash (Monthly) = 3 units = 3 $\times$ 9,000 = 27,000.
Yash (Annual) = 27,000 $\times$ 12 = 3,24,000.

Exam Takeaway: Method 1 is the safest and fastest here. SSC CGL examiner humesha 'Monthly' aur 'Annual' keywords ke beech me jalebi banata hai. Screen par question padhte waqt aankho se 'Monthly/Annual' ko underline karne ki aadat daal.

questions.q: If the first number is 15% less than the third number and the ratio of the second and third numbers is 3 : 5, then by what percentage is the average of the first and third numbers more than the second number?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, sabse best aur safe tareeka hai ki Third number ko seedha $100$ maan le. Isse tera base set ho jayega aur saari calculations makhan ki tarah smooth ho jayengi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Base ko $100$ maan aur direct ratio shift karke values nikal le!

$$T = 100 \implies F = 85$$
$$S:T = 3:5 \implies 5u = 100 \implies 1u = 20 \implies S = 60$$
$$\text{Avg}(F,T) = \frac{85+100}{2} = 92.5$$
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{92.5-60}{60} \times 100 = \frac{32.5}{60} \times 100 = 54.16\%$$

Mathematically :-
$$z = x, \ y = 0.85x, \ y:z = 3:5 \dots$$

$$\text{New Exp} = 203 \times 86.1 = 17,478.3$$
$$\text{Difference} = 17,478.3 - 16,646 = 832.3$$

questions.q: If Aman's salary is $12 \%$ more than Bhuvan's salary, by how much percent is Bhuvan's salary less than that of Aman?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: CPR

Pen-Free Observation: $12 \%$ yani $3/25$ ka increase hai. CPR rule se agar value $x/y$ badhti hai, toh return journey me $x/(x+y)$ girti hai. Seedha $3/28$ karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Constant Product Ratio (CPR) se directly base shift calculate karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \uparrow \text{Increase} = 12 \% = \frac{3}{25} \\ \downarrow \text{Decrease} = \frac{3}{25+3} = \frac{3}{28} \\ \downarrow \% = \frac{3}{28} \times 100 = \frac{75}{7} \% = 10.71 \% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio banakar base change karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let Bhuvan} = 100 \\ \text{Aman} = 100 + 12 = 112 \\ \text{Difference} = 12 \\ \text{Bhuvan is less by} = \frac{12}{112} \times 100 \\ = \frac{3}{28} \times 100 = 10.71 \% $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha fractional changes use karo. $A$ is more than $B$ by $a/b$, then $B$ is less than $A$ by $a/(a+b)$.

questions.q: If 20% of X is added to 75% of X then the results become (X-21)% of 200 then find the value of 250% of X?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, LHS ban gaya $95\%$ of X. Aur RHS pe 200 ka koi bhi percentage seedha double ho jata hai. Ek line ki aasan equation banegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Zeroes hata kar decimals ki sidhi equation bana aur target nikal. Mathematically :-

$0.95X = 2(X - 21)$

$0.95X = 2X - 42$

$1.05X = 42 \Rightarrow X = 40$

$Target = 2.5 \times 40 = 100$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pura percentage solve kar step by step. Mathematically :-

$\frac{20X}{100} + \frac{75X}{100} = \frac{(X-21)}{100} \times 200$

$\frac{95X}{100} = 2X - 42$

$\frac{105X}{100} = 42 \Rightarrow X = 40$

$\frac{250}{100} \times 40 = 100$

Exam Takeaway: Percentage of 200 jaisi cheezon ko sidha multiply by 2 socha kar, steps likh ke time waste mat kar.

questions.q: Due to a reduction of $50 \text{ paise}$ per dozen in the price of bananas, Rohan can buy 1 dozen more bananas for Rs. 66. What is the original price of bananas per dozen?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: CPR

Pen-Free Observation: Price gira toh consumption badhi. Quadratic equation banane ki bajaye, Rs. 66 ke perfect divisors options me dhundo jinme 0.5 ka gap rakhne par quantity ka gap 1 dozen aaye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Option verification is the king here. Seedha $66/x$ check karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Check Option C (Rs. 6 /dozen)} \\ \text{Initial Qty} = \frac{66}{6} = 11 \text{ dozen} \\ \text{New Price} = 6 - 0.5 = 5.5 \text{ Rs/dozen} \\ \text{New Qty} = \frac{66}{5.5} = \frac{660}{55} = 12 \text{ dozen} \\ \text{Difference} = 12 - 11 = 1 \text{ dozen (Matches condition)} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Basic price and quantity relation likho aur quadratic equation solve karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let original price} = P \\ \frac{66}{P - 0.5} - \frac{66}{P} = 1 \\ 66P - 66(P - 0.5) = P(P - 0.5) \\ 33 = P^2 - 0.5P \\ 2P^2 - P - 66 = 0 \\ (P - 6)(2P + 11) = 0 \implies P = 6 $$

Exam Takeaway: Total expenditure constant wale sawalo me agar quantity gap diya ho, toh hamesha Options uthao, $99 \%$ times answers perfectly divide karte hain total amount ko.

OptionCalculation
Rs. 6$66/6=11 \rightarrow 66/5.5=12$ (Diff 1)

questions.q: Vasu gave 12000 of the amount what he had to Nithi. Nithi gave 3/5th of what he received from Vasu to Sara. Sara after paying Rs. 500 to the taxi driver out of the amount she get from Nithi, Sara is now left with Rs. x+300. Find square root of x.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai TestRipper, yahan ek sequence me paise transfer ho rahe hain aur last ka bacha hua part $x+300$ diya hai. Option dekh, saare perfect squares hain. Seedha reverse chal aur mental maths se minus karta jaa.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Ulta chalte hain (Reverse calculation) without wasting ink.

Mathematically :-
$$12000 \times \frac{3}{5} = 7200 \\\\ 7200 - 500 = 6700 \\\\ x + 300 = 6700 \\\\ x = 6400 \\\\ \sqrt{x} = 80$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Step by step variables assign karke values nikalte hain.

Mathematically :-
$$Amount_{Nithi} = 12000 \\\\ Amount_{Sara} = 12000 \times \frac{3}{5} = 7200 \\\\ Balance_{Sara} = 7200 - 500 = 6700 \\\\ x + 300 = 6700 \Rightarrow x = 6400 \\\\ \sqrt{x} = 80$$

Exam Takeaway: Jab value transfer ho rahi ho step-by-step, toh chain sequence follow karke end result nikalna sabse easy hota hai. Pen kam chalao.

questions.q: In an examination, Ravi scores $40\%$ marks and fails by 30 marks. In the same examination, Sohan scores $50\%$ marks and gets 20 marks more than the minimum pass marks. Find the maximum marks of the examination.
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, number line soch. Pass mark beech mein hai. Ravi $40\%$ lakar 30 peeche reh gaya (-30). Sohan $50\%$ lakar 20 aage nikal gaya (+20). Dono ke percentage ka gap = $10\%$. Aur marks ka gap = $50$. Zero calculation, total visualization!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ (50\% - 40\%) \times \text{Max} = 30 + 20 \\ 10\% \times \text{Max} = 50 \\ \text{Max} = 50 \times 10 = 500 $$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha percentages ka difference = pass-fail ke marks ka sum karna hai aise conditions me.

questions.q: The count of bacteria in a sample grows by 24% during the first hour. It decreases by 15% during the next one hour and again decreases by 10% during the third hour. If the present count of bacteria in the sample is 55000, then what will be the net increase/decrease in the count of bacteria after three hours?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Isme bhi wahi successive wala lagega but reduced part nahi nikalata toh hume final nikal ke intial se subtract karna hi padega. Final answer tab nikalega jab numbers jinke end me 1, 7, aur 9 aate hain wo multiply honge. Unit digit method humari mehnat bacha lega bina pura solve kiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai, seedha base shift mar.
Final Count $= 55000 \times \frac{124}{100} \times \frac{85}{100} \times \frac{90}{100}$.
$$ = 55000 \times \frac{31}{25} \times \frac{17}{20} \times \frac{9}{10} = 11 \times 31 \times 17 \times 9$$
Ab pura guna mat karna. Last digit check kar: $1 \times 1 \times 7 \times 9 = 3$.
Final count ke aakhiri me 3 aayega. Start 55000 (yani 0) se tha. Decrease $= 10 - 3 = 7$. Jiske aakhiri me 7 hai wahi tera answer hai, yani 2827. Since $11 \times 31 \times 17 \times 9 = 52173$ (chota ho gaya), ye decrease hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractions like $\frac{124}{100} = \frac{31}{25}$ use karne se numerator chote rehte hain aur zeroes properly cancel ho jaate hain.

Exam Takeaway: Jab options ke unit digits alag hon, toh puri calculation karne wala gadha hota hai. Unit digit is a god-tier hack.

questions.q: Every day a fruit seller sells 66.67% of the fruits he has and 50% of the fruits rot overnight. If a total of 688 fruits rot in three nights, then how many fruits did he start with on the first day.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fraction ka jaal hai. $2/3$ sell hue, bache $1/3$. Unka $50\% (1/2)$ sad gaye. Har din $1/6$ sadenge. Options me aakhri digits alag hain. Unit digit trick laga kar seedha attack hoga bina heavy calc ke.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Denominators ka LCM initial value assume karo aur tree method banao, unit digit verify karo.

Mathematically :-
$$Total = 6 \times 6 \times 6 = 216 \\\\ Rot_{Day1} = 216 \times \frac{1}{6} = 36 \\\\ Rot_{Day2} = 36 \times \frac{1}{6} = 6 \\\\ Rot_{Day3} = 6 \times \frac{1}{6} = 1 \\\\ Total \ Rot = 36 + 6 + 1 = 43 \\\\ 43 \ units = 688 \Rightarrow 1 \ unit = 16 \\\\ Total = 216 \times 16 = 3456$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variable x rakh kar fraction addition karo.

Mathematically :-
$$Total = x \\\\ Rot = x \times \frac{1}{6} + (x \times \frac{1}{6}) \times \frac{1}{6} + ((x \times \frac{1}{6}) \times \frac{1}{6}) \times \frac{1}{6} = 688 \\\\ x(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{36} + \frac{1}{216}) = 688 \\\\ x(\frac{43}{216}) = 688 \Rightarrow x = 3456$$

Exam Takeaway: Tree method lagana aur fractional denominators ka LCM initial value assume karna is best for remaining items questions.

List IList II
Unit Digit Check$216 \times 16 \Rightarrow 6 \times 6 = 36$, Ends with $6$.

Mathematically :-

$$ 41 \frac{2}{3}\% = \frac{5}{12} \\ I_1 = 12x, I_2 = 17x \\ 0.9(17x + 92000) = 3(12x) \\ 17x + 92000 = 40x \\ 23x = 92000 \\ x = 4000 \\ Inc = 5x = 20000 $$

Mathematically :-

$$ \frac{10P}{3} - \frac{17P}{12} = 92000 \\ \frac{23P}{12} = 92000 \\ P = 48000 \\ Inc = \frac{5}{12} \times 48000 = 20000 $$

questions.q: The income of person X is $60 \%$ less than that of person Y, and the expenditure of X is equal to $60 \%$ of Y's expenditure. If X's income is equal to $70 \%$ of Y's expenditure, then what is the ratio of the savings of X and Y?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Cross-Product

Pen-Free Observation: Y ki expenditure ko aisi value maan jiska percentage aaram se nikle, jaise 400. Sab us par depend kar raha hai, bina $x$ liye directly saari values integer me aayengi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Kisi ek independent base ko 100 ka multiple maan kar saari values nikal lo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let } E_Y = 400 \\ I_X = 70 \% \text{ of } 400 = 280 \\ E_X = 60 \% \text{ of } 400 = 240 \\ S_X = 280 - 240 = 40 \\ \text{Now, } I_X \text{ is } 60 \% \text{ less than } I_Y \implies I_X = 40 \% \text{ of } I_Y \\ 280 = 0.4 \times I_Y \implies I_Y = 700 \\ S_Y = 700 - 400 = 300 \\ \text{Ratio } S_X : S_Y = 40 : 300 = 2 : 15 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratios aur variables se step by step balance kar sakte ho par fractions me atakne ka risk hota hai.

Mathematically :-

$$ I_X = 0.4 I_Y \\ E_X = 0.6 E_Y \\ I_X = 0.7 E_Y \\ 0.4 I_Y = 0.7 E_Y \implies \frac{I_Y}{E_Y} = \frac{7}{4} \\ \text{Let } I_Y = 700k, E_Y = 400k \\ I_X = 0.7(400k) = 280k \\ E_X = 0.6(400k) = 240k \\ S_X = 40k \\ S_Y = 700k - 400k = 300k \\ \frac{S_X}{S_Y} = \frac{40k}{300k} = \frac{2}{15} $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise multiple ratio wale questions me linking variable ko pakda kar. Yahan $I_X$ dono conditions ko connect kar raha tha, wahi se calculation start karni thi.

questions.q: A businessman donates $30 \%$ of his total wealth to an NGO. He gives $30 \%$ and $25 \%$ of the remaining wealth to his wife and son respectively. The rest he divides equally among his three daughters. If one of his daughters gets Rs. 42 lakh as her share, what was the businessman's total wealth (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: $30 \%$ gaya, bacha $70 \%$. Ab iska $55 \%$ bhi gaya ($30 \% + 25 \%$). Toh bacha bas $45 \%$ of $70 \%$. Ye 3 betiyon me barabar batega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Successive ka direct tree branch nikalo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Total Wealth} = 100 \% \\ \text{NGO} = 30 \%, \text{ Remaining} = 70 \% \\ \text{Wife + Son} = (30 \% + 25 \%) \text{ of } 70 \% = 55 \% \text{ of } 70 \% \\ \text{Daughters (Total)} = (100 \% - 55 \%) \text{ of } 70 \% = 45 \% \text{ of } 70 \% = 31.5 \% \\ \text{Each Daughter} = \frac{31.5 \%}{3} = 10.5 \% \\ 10.5 \% = 42 \text{ Lakh} \\ 1 \% = 4 \text{ Lakh} \implies 100 \% = 400 \text{ Lakh} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fraction chain se variables man kar multiply karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let total wealth} = W \\ \text{After NGO} = W \times 0.7 \\ \text{After Wife & Son} = W \times 0.7 \times (1 - 0.55) = W \times 0.7 \times 0.45 \\ \text{One Daughter} = \frac{W \times 0.7 \times 0.45}{3} \\ \frac{W \times 0.315}{3} = 42 \\ W \times 0.105 = 42 \implies W = \frac{42}{0.105} = 400 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab word remaining likha ho toh branch hamesha nayi start hoti hai. Wife aur son dono ko remaining ka common percent mil raha tha isliye wo mathematically add hokar $55 \%$ ban gaye.

He followed the same procedure with the remaining capital after the second and the third year. Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (CI, Area, Successive discounts)

Dimag me seedha fraction soch: Ek taraf se 7/5 ban raha hai aur dusri taraf se 6/7. Dono multiply honge toh 7 se 7 katega aur bas 6/5 bachega. Ye observation exam me tere 20 second bachayegi!

$$40\% = \frac{2}{5} \implies \frac{7}{5}$$
$$14.28\% = \frac{1}{7} \implies \frac{6}{7}$$

$$X \times \frac{216}{125} = 4320$$
$$X = 20 \times 125 = 2500$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Decimal method ka time waste trial. Jab fractions aapas me kategi nahi tabhi ye approach use karna.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Net} = 1.4 \times \frac{6}{7} = 1.2$$
$$X \times (1.2)^3 = 4320$$
$$X \times 1.728 = 4320 \implies 2500$$

Exam Takeaway: Hamesha fractions (Ratios) me khelo jab tak specifically ajeeb decimal values na di hon. Successive operations me numerators aur denominators aksar cross-cancel ho jate hain, jo calculation ko ekdum zero kar dete hain.

$$300 - 3x = 100 + x \implies 4x = 200 \implies x = 50$$

$$\text{P2} = 65\% \times 200 = 130$$
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{360 - 130}{130} \times 100 = \frac{230}{130} \times 100 \approx 176.9\% \approx 177\%$$

Mathematically :-
$$120(1 - x) = 40(1 + x) \dots$$

questions.q: A’s salary is 120% of B’s salary and B spends 60% of his salary for house rent and education fees. If B’s savings is Rs. 1800 and A’s expenditure is 40% more than that of B, then what is the saving amount of A?
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, seedha B ki savings (absolute value) de rakhi hai aur saara percentage flow ek dusre se linked hai. Aise continuous sequence me variables ($x, y$) lene ki zarurat hi nahi hoti. Base $100$ pakdo aur seedha line se link karte hue A ki savings tak pahunch jao!

**Method 1 (Base $100$ / Exam Approach):**
Maan lo B ki Income = $100$ units.
Toh A ki Income = $120$ units.
B ka Expenditure = $60$ units, matlab B ki Savings = $40$ units.
A ka Expenditure = $40\%$ zyada hai B ke expenditure se = $60 + (60 \times \frac{40}{100}) = 84$ units.
A ki Savings = $120 - 84 = 36$ units.

Question ke hisaab se: B ki savings $40 \text{ units} \equiv 1800$
$1 \text{ unit} \equiv 45$
A ki savings = $36 \text{ units} = 36 \times 45 = 1620$.

**Method 2 (Ratio / Concept Builder):**
Salary ratio A:B = $120:100 = 6:5$.
B ka Exp : Savings = $60:40 = 3:2$.
Humein pata hai B ki Savings ($2 \text{ units}$) = $1800 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 900$.
Yahan se B ki Salary ($5 \text{ units}$) = $4500$, aur B ka Exp ($3 \text{ units}$) = $2700$.
Ratio se A ki Salary = $6 \times 900 = 5400$.
A ka Exp $40\%$ zyada hai B ke Exp ($2700$) se = $2700 \times 1.4 = 3780$.
A ki Savings = $5400 - 3780 = 1620$.


🏆 **Exam Takeaway: Kab Kya Lagana Hai? (The Thumb Rule)**

$0.148x = 185$

$x = \frac{185}{0.148} = 1250$

questions_hin.q_hi: In a corporate restructuring, the total number of employees in Division A and Division B remains strictly constant. Initially, Division A has '$x$' more employees than Division B, and it is given that Division A has exactly $13x$ employees. After a transfer drive, Division B becomes the majority with '$5x$' more employees than Division A. Meanwhile, the average revenue generated per employee in Division B increased from ₹7,12,400 to ₹8,54,880. What is the exact percentage change in the total revenue generated by Division B?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM (Constant Sum Shifting) + Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yeh hai TCS ka asli jaal! Total Revenue = (No. of Employees) $\times$ (Revenue per Employee). Yahan multiply ho raha hai, toh end mein Successive (Theory 2) lagega. Lekin Division B ke employees ka increase directly nahi diya, usko unhone Theory 1 ($A+B=K$) mein chhupa diya hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dono ka percentage shift nikal aur formula me daal de! Employee shift JSM se find kar, baki direct observation.

Mathematically :-
$$ A - B = x \\implies B = 13x - x = 12x \\\\ Gap = x - (-5x) = 6x \\\\ \\Delta Emp = \\frac{6x}{2} = 3x \\\\ \\% \\Delta Emp = \\frac{3x}{12x} = 25\\% \\\\ \\% \\Delta Rev/Emp = \\frac{854880 - 712400}{712400} = 20\\% \\\\ Net = 25 + 20 + \\frac{25 \\times 20}{100} = 50\\% $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute revenue variables generate kar initial stage aur final stage me aur shift detect kar.

Mathematically :-
$$ Rev_1 = 12x \\times 712400 \\\\ Rev_2 = 15x \\times 854880 \\\\ \\frac{Rev_2}{Rev_1} = \\frac{15}{12} \\times \\frac{854880}{712400} = 1.25 \\times 1.2 = 1.5 \\\\ \\Delta = 50\\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi do concepts mix hon, unko isolation mein solve kar. Total number ya exact variables ($x$) nikalne ki koshish mat kar, hamesha base fractional values aur percentages pe khel.

questions_hin.q_hi:
A massive commercial cargo ship has a strictly fixed maximum payload capacity dedicated entirely to carrying only two types of containers: Type-A (Chemicals) and Type-B (Textiles). The total payload weight of a container type is determined by multiplying the "Weight per container" by the "Number of containers". Initially, the total payload weight of Type-A was exactly 33.33% of the total payload weight of Type-B.

Due to new safety regulations, the weight of "each" Type-A container is increased by 15%, while the company strictly keeps the number of Type-A containers unchanged. To keep the ship's total payload weight exactly at its fixed maximum capacity, by what percentage must the overall payload weight of Type-B containers be reduced?
questions_hin.s_hi: Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: Layer 1: Constant Base Expansion: Weight/Box $\times$ No. of Boxes = Total Weight ($A \times B = K$). Layer 2: JSM / The Zero-Sum Game: Total Weight A + Total Weight B = Fixed Ship Capacity ($A + B = K$). The "Pen-Free" Observation First: Dekh bhai, dimaag ko bilkul shant rakh. SSC wale language badal ke darayenge, par core engine wahi hai. Type-A containers $33.33\%$ hain Type-B ke. Yani Ratio $1:3$ hai. Type-A ke har ek dabbe ka wazan $15\%$ badha aur dabbon ki sankhya same rahi (Layer 1). Iska seedha sa matlab hai ki Type-A ka Total Wazan exact $15\%$ se badh gaya! Ab total jahaz ka wazan fix rakhna hai, toh Type-A ne jitna wazan badhaya, Type-B ko exactly utna hi wazan kam karna padega (Layer 2). 10 second ka game hai! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Ratio Balancer): Ratio of Total Weights $\rightarrow$ Type-A : Type-B = $1 : 3$. Type-A ka naya gain = $1$ unit ka $15\%$ = $+0.15$ units. Kyuki Jahaz ka total wazan (Capacity) fix hai, jo wazan Type-A ne gain kiya, wo Type-B ko lose karna padega. Type-B ka reduction = $-0.15$ units. Percentage Reduction in Type-B = $\frac{\text{Actual Reduction}}{\text{Type-B Base}} \times 100$ $\Rightarrow \frac{0.15}{3} \times 100 =$ $5\%$. Option 2 is strictly correct. Method 2 (Concept Builder - Assumption Method): Let Total Weight of Type-B = $300$ tons. Since Type-A is $33.33\%$ (or $1/3$) of B, Type-A = $100$ tons. Total Ship Capacity = $100 + 300 = 400$ tons. Type-A ka wazan $15\%$ badh gaya $\Rightarrow$ Naya Type-A = $115$ tons. Ship capacity $400$ fix rakhni hai, toh Naya Type-B = $400 - 115 = 285$ tons. Type-B mein kitni girawat aayi? $300 \rightarrow 285$, yani $15$ tons ki girawat aayi $300$ par. Percentage = $\frac{15}{300} \times 100 =$ $5\%$. Future Exam Takeaway: Language chahe "Cargo Capacity" ki ho ya "Server/Data Bandwidth" ki, agar ek component $A \times B$ se bana hai aur unka overall sum fixed hai, toh direct base ratio likho aur shift ko transfer kar do. Ye Double-Engine hacks hi top rankers ka secret weapon hain!

questions_hin.q_hi: The present population of a village is 45,840. If the number of males increases by $25\%$ and that of females increases by $15\%$, then the population will become 55,284. What is the difference between the initial number of males and females in the village?
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, isme Mixture Alligation ya phir Base Shifting lagate hain. Maan le pura gaon hi $15\%$ se badh gaya hota. Total kitna badhta? Jo extra badha hai woh sirf Males ke bache hue $10\%$ ka kamaal hai.

Method 1 (Base Shifting Concept):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Actual Increase} = 55284 - 45840 = 9444 \\ \text{Base } 15\% \text{ Increase} = 45840 \times 15\% = 6876 \\ \text{Extra Increase} = 9444 - 6876 = 2568 \\ 10\% \text{ of } M = 2568 \implies M = 25680 \\ F = 45840 - 25680 = 20160 \\ M - F = 25680 - 20160 = 5520 $$

Exam Takeaway: Base Shifting wali trick CDS aur CGL dono ke time consuming mixture problems ko crush karti hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: Sushil's monthly salary is 20% of Pankaj's annual salary. Yash's monthly salary is 3/4th of Sushil's monthly salary. If the monthly salary of Pankaj is Rs 15000, what is the annual salary of Yash?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling (Equating units to real values)

Pen-Free Observation: Pankaj ki monthly 15k hai, toh chain reaction me Yash ki annual kafi badi aayegi. Pura khela sirf clear base-shifting ka hai. Question ke keywords 'Monthly' aur 'Annual' ko dhyan se dekhna hai aur single line me execution karna hai. Maximum bacche ratio me Pankaj ki annual value ko uski monthly se equate karke Concept Leakage kar dete hain!

Method 1 (The Chain Reaction - Exam Approach):
Aise simple chain problems me ratio banake time waste mat kar. Jab clear percentage aur fraction diye hon, toh peeche se single line execution kar:
  • Pankaj (Monthly) = 15,000
  • Pankaj (Annual) = 15,000 $\times$ 12 = 1,80,000
  • Sushil (Monthly) = 20% of Pankaj (Annual) = $\frac{1}{5} \times 1,80,000 = 36,000$
  • Yash (Monthly) = $\frac{3}{4}$ of Sushil (Monthly) = $\frac{3}{4} \times 36,000 = 27,000$
  • Yash (Annual) = 27,000 $\times$ 12 = 3,24,000


Method 2 (Ratio Scaling Correction):
Agar tu ratio banata hai $S : P(\text{Annual}) : Y = 4 : 20 : 3$, toh yaad rakh 20 units Pankaj ki Annual salary hai, monthly nahi.
Pankaj (Annual) = 15,000 $\times$ 12 = 1,80,000.
So, 20 units = 1,80,000 $\implies$ 1 unit = 9,000.
Yash (Monthly) = 3 units = 3 $\times$ 9,000 = 27,000.
Yash (Annual) = 27,000 $\times$ 12 = 3,24,000.

Exam Takeaway: Method 1 is the safest and fastest here. SSC CGL examiner humesha 'Monthly' aur 'Annual' keywords ke beech me jalebi banata hai. Screen par question padhte waqt aankho se 'Monthly/Annual' ko underline karne ki aadat daal.

questions_hin.q_hi: The price of petrol shot up by 5%. Before the hike, the price was Rs. 82 per litre. A man travels 3045 km every month and his car gives mileage of 15 km per litre. What is the increase the monthly expenditure (to the nearest Rs.) on the man's travel due to the hike in the petrol in prices?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, gadhe bachhe pura purana kharcha nikalenge aur phir naya kharcha nikal ke minus karenge. Apne ko smart banna hai! Sirf 'increase' pucha hai, toh sirf 'increased price' wale difference pe dhyan de.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Petrol ki extra badhi hui keemat nikal aur seedha total consumption se multiply mar de!

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Extra Rate} = 82 \times 5\% = 4.1$$
$$\text{Total Litres} = \frac{3045}{15} = 203$$
$$\text{Extra Exp.} = 203 \times 4.1 = 832.3 \approx 832$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Old expenditure aur New expenditure alag alag nikal ke minus kar.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Old Exp} = 203 \times 82 = 16,646$$

questions_hin.q_hi: The income of person X is $60 \%$ less than that of person Y, and the expenditure of X is equal to $60 \%$ of Y's expenditure. If X's income is equal to $70 \%$ of Y's expenditure, then what is the ratio of the savings of X and Y?

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Kisi ek independent base ko 100 ka multiple maan kar saari values nikal lo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let } E_Y = 400 \\ I_X = 70 \% \text{ of } 400 = 280 \\ E_X = 60 \% \text{ of } 400 = 240 \\ S_X = 280 - 240 = 40 \\ \text{Now, } I_X \text{ is } 60 \% \text{ less than } I_Y \implies I_X = 40 \% \text{ of } I_Y \\ 280 = 0.4 \times I_Y \implies I_Y = 700 \\ S_Y = 700 - 400 = 300 \\ \text{Ratio } S_X : S_Y = 40 : 300 = 2 : 15 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratios aur variables se step by step balance kar sakte ho par fractions me atakne ka risk hota hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: A businessman donates $30 \%$ of his total wealth to an NGO. He gives $30 \%$ and $25 \%$ of the remaining wealth to his wife and son respectively. The rest he divides equally among his three daughters. If one of his daughters gets Rs. 42 lakh as her share, what was the businessman's total wealth (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change

Pen-Free Observation: $30 \%$ gaya, bacha $70 \%$. Ab iska $55 \%$ bhi gaya ($30 \% + 25 \%$). Toh bacha bas $45 \%$ of $70 \%$. Ye 3 betiyon me barabar batega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Successive ka direct tree branch nikalo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Total Wealth} = 100 \% \\ \text{NGO} = 30 \%, \text{ Remaining} = 70 \% \\ \text{Wife + Son} = (30 \% + 25 \%) \text{ of } 70 \% = 55 \% \text{ of } 70 \% \\ \text{Daughters (Total)} = (100 \% - 55 \%) \text{ of } 70 \% = 45 \% \text{ of } 70 \% = 31.5 \% \\ \text{Each Daughter} = \frac{31.5 \%}{3} = 10.5 \% \\ 10.5 \% = 42 \text{ Lakh} \\ 1 \% = 4 \text{ Lakh} \implies 100 \% = 400 \text{ Lakh} $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fraction chain se variables man kar multiply karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Let total wealth} = W \\ \text{After NGO} = W \times 0.7 \\ \text{After Wife & Son} = W \times 0.7 \times (1 - 0.55) = W \times 0.7 \times 0.45 \\ \text{One Daughter} = \frac{W \times 0.7 \times 0.45}{3} \\ \frac{W \times 0.315}{3} = 42 \\ W \times 0.105 = 42 \implies W = \frac{42}{0.105} = 400 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab word remaining likha ho toh branch hamesha nayi start hoti hai. Wife aur son dono ko remaining ka common percent mil raha tha isliye wo mathematically add hokar $55 \%$ ban gaye.

questions_hin.q_hi: A’s salary is 120% of B’s salary and B spends 60% of his salary for house rent and education fees. If B’s savings is Rs. 1800 and A’s expenditure is 40% more than that of B, then what is the saving amount of A?
questions_hin.s_hi:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, seedha B ki savings (absolute value) de rakhi hai aur saara percentage flow ek dusre se linked hai. Aise continuous sequence me variables ($x, y$) lene ki zarurat hi nahi hoti. Base $100$ pakdo aur seedha line se link karte hue A ki savings tak pahunch jao!

**Method 1 (Base $100$ / Exam Approach):**
Maan lo B ki Income = $100$ units.
Toh A ki Income = $120$ units.
B ka Expenditure = $60$ units, matlab B ki Savings = $40$ units.
A ka Expenditure = $40\%$ zyada hai B ke expenditure se = $60 + (60 \times \frac{40}{100}) = 84$ units.
A ki Savings = $120 - 84 = 36$ units.

Question ke hisaab se: B ki savings $40 \text{ units} \equiv 1800$
$1 \text{ unit} \equiv 45$
A ki savings = $36 \text{ units} = 36 \times 45 = 1620$.

**Method 2 (Ratio / Concept Builder):**
Salary ratio A:B = $120:100 = 6:5$.
B ka Exp : Savings = $60:40 = 3:2$.
Humein pata hai B ki Savings ($2 \text{ units}$) = $1800 \implies 1 \text{ unit} = 900$.
Yahan se B ki Salary ($5 \text{ units}$) = $4500$, aur B ka Exp ($3 \text{ units}$) = $2700$.
Ratio se A ki Salary = $6 \times 900 = 5400$.
A ka Exp $40\%$ zyada hai B ke Exp ($2700$) se = $2700 \times 1.4 = 3780$.
A ki Savings = $5400 - 3780 = 1620$.
